title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in a residential Austin neighborhood while in autonomous mode, with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop for the duck, which was nesting outside a local restaurant and known to residents. This shows a failure in object detection or decision-making at the level of individual animals in pedestrian environments, a category of obstacle that the system either did not identify or did not treat as requiring avoidance.

A human safety operator was present during the incident but did not intervene. Whether the operator could have seen and stopped the vehicle in time is not established. Catching this failure would have required either better model performance on small animals, or a testing and simulation process that identified this gap before deployment in areas where wildlife was present.

A resident claimed the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign; Avride's review of the vehicle's data contradicted this claim, and the accuracy of either account is not established. The company responded by excluding certain streets from service and by running simulations to prevent similar incidents.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck was nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant and had become familiar to neighborhood residents, which intensified their concerns about autonomous vehicle safety in residential areas.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode at the time. A resident also claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride stated their review of vehicle data found no evidence supporting this claim. In response, Avride has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake from its service area. The company is now evaluating technological improvements through simulated experiments to prevent similar incidents while maintaining safety performance in other scenarios. Local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator.
